name: Existing Project Analysis
purpose: Perform deep, non-destructive reconnaissance on an existing codebase to detect architecture, build systems, conventions, tech debt, and drift.
whenToUse: Onboarding an established repository into Project Intelligence governance
Detecting architectural patterns, conventions, and existing dependencies prior to feature work
Auditing technical debt, uncommitted changes, or state drift in legacy codebases
Evaluating test suite maturity and build pipeline commands on existing projects
prerequisites: Existing codebase with filesystem read access
Installed Git CLI with repository history access
Read access to existing configuration and package manifests

inputs.name: projectRoot
inputs.description: Path to the existing repository root

inputs.name: deepScanDepth
inputs.description: Maximum directory traversal depth for file tree mapping

inputs.name: excludePatterns
inputs.description: Directory or file patterns to ignore during analysis (e.g., node_modules, .git, venv)

procedure.title: Directory Tree and Manifest Scanning
procedure.action: Enumerate top-level directory structure and parse key build/package manifests (package.json, pyproject.toml, go.mod, Cargo.toml, pom.xml, CMakeLists.txt).

procedure.title: Coding Convention and Linter Detection
procedure.action: Identify formatting, linting, and style configuration files (.eslintrc, ruff.toml, prettierrc, tsconfig.json). Extract existing coding conventions.

procedure.title: Build, Test, and CI Pipeline Analysis
procedure.action: Locate test suites and CI workflows (.github/workflows, Jenkinsfile, Makefile, docker-compose.yml). Identify how tests are invoked and execution requirements.

procedure.title: Git History and Hotspot Mapping
procedure.action: Inspect git log history to detect frequently modified files, recent author commits, unmerged branches, and existing architectural documentation (ADRs, docs/).

procedure.title: Technical Debt and Anti-Pattern Audit
procedure.action: Identify unresolved TODO/FIXME markers, deprecated library usages, missing test coverage areas, and obvious architectural smells.

procedure.title: Memory State Ingestion
procedure.action: Populate memory/state.json with durableKnowledge (discovered conventions, architectural decisions, domain vocabulary) and backlogAndHistory (technical debt).

expectedOutputs: Comprehensive architecture and convention reconnaissance report
Updated memory/state.json with extracted codingConventions and technicalDebt entries
Baseline requirements and constraints documentation for contract formulation

potentialFailures: Repository too massive leading to timeout during full traversal
Multiple conflicting build tools or monorepo subprojects
failureAndRecovery.recoveryStrategy: Apply targeted subtree scanning focusing on src/ or core packages. If monorepo detected, analyze root manifest first, then partition analysis into distinct sub-packages. For shallow git clones, report limited history in findings.

verificationCriteria: All detected build and test commands are validated by checking corresponding config files
Existing conventions are documented in memory without overwriting user rules
No files outside memory/ or reports are modified during analysis (strictly non-destructive)
Identified technical debt items are tagged with severity and location
